paths.description: Representative unknown route to inspect HTTP and recovery behaviour.

findings.summary: The site is hard-coded dark rather than responding to the user’s colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Evaluate probes under prefers-color-scheme light and dark both returned body background rgb(0,0,0), text rgb(246,244,234), and computed color-scheme “normal”.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare an appropriate color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens so browser chrome and surfaces honour the selected scheme.

findings.summary: The mobile navigation transition has no reduced-motion override.
findings.evidence: DOM CSS contains 0.3s transitions for mobile navigation, while the reduced-motion probe found no prefers-reduced-motion rule; the drawer still changed to left:0 under the reduce condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential drawer transitions in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and make the reduced state immediate.

findings.summary: MPA route changes are abrupt and do not use cross-document View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection found no view-transition-name or @view-transition rules across home, category, and detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for shared page chrome, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The very long listing has fixed mobile chrome with no scroll-state response or progress affordance.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout measured a 32,611px document; CSS inspection found no scroll-state container query or progress indicator, while #mobtop remains position:fixed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query to compact or hide non-essential header chrome after scrolling, and expose a lightweight progress/return affordance.

findings.summary: The mobile navigation drawer is an ad-hoc div overlay without a semantic dismissible primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS shows #mobmenu, #statpart, and .closepart divs moved by class/left positioning; there is no dialog, popover, or details element.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the drawer as a semantic dialog or popover with declarative invocation, light-dismiss, focus management, and an explicitly named close button.

findings.summary: Reusable video cards respond only to global viewport breakpoints, not their container.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found many @media breakpoints for .list_videos .item but zero @container rules, despite cards appearing in main, category, and related-content contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Give card grids an inline-size containment context and move card-level layout changes to @container rules, retaining viewport fallbacks as needed.

findings.summary: Core mobile menu and search affordances are styled div/icon controls rather than keyboard-operable controls.
findings.evidence: The mobile screenshot shows hamburger/search controls, but the focus probe’s 302 focusable controls excludes .mobver/.mobsearch; CSS identifies these as cursor:pointer elements and DOM semantics provide no button role.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real button elements with accessible names, visible focus, and at least 44x44 CSS-pixel targets; retain click behaviour and add keyboard-tested focus management.

findings.summary: Large layout shifts make the page visually unstable.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive measured CLS 0.810 with two shifts near 2.18s; Lighthouse corroborated CLS 0.825 while LCP was 1.7s and TBT 0ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/card geometry before load with width/height or aspect-ratio, and ensure lazy placeholders and final thumbnails occupy identical boxes.

findings.summary: Seven classic scripts are parser-inserted without async, defer, or module semantics.
findings.evidence: HAR summary identified the stylesheet plus seven scripts as render-blocking candidates; DOM confirmation shows pab-ssl.js, xedo pub.js, jQuery 2.1.3, notify, user, ajax, and counter scripts without async/defer/type=module. jQuery was the largest transfer at 33,937 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical first-party scripts, load advertising/analytics after consent or interaction, and remove or replace legacy jQuery dependencies where feasible.

findings.summary: Some controls and imagery lack robust accessible semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility score was 0.71 and flagged the footer arrow image with no alt; DOM inspection also found custom mobile menu/search controls with no native role or accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic buttons for controls, provide concise accessible names, and add meaningful alt text or alt="" for decorative images.

findings.summary: Pages have no semantic main or navigation landmarks, and core mobile controls are outside the focus order.
findings.evidence: The evaluate probe found no header/nav/main/aside/footer landmarks; Lighthouse explicitly failed landmark-one-main. Focus probing found default outlines on links but did not reach the hamburger/search div controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce header, nav, main, aside, and footer landmarks; make all controls native focusable elements and verify logical focus order through the drawer and video actions.

findings.summary: The viewport caps zoom and the primary video has no caption track.
findings.evidence: The viewport is maximum-scale=1.0, which Lighthouse flags as limiting zoom below 5; the representative detail probe found a user-facing video with controls but zero track elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale, preserve user scaling, and provide accurate WebVTT captions or an equivalent transcript for video content.

findings.summary: Image markup omits intrinsic dimensions and responsive variants.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reported 100/100 sampled images without width/height, 97 without srcset, and 100 legacy-format files; Lighthouse also found thumbnails displayed at 400x225 from 320x180 sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height on every image, provide correctly sized srcset/sizes variants, and avoid upscaling low-resolution thumbnails.

findings.summary: Public templates omit canonical URLs and the advertised site has no sitemap at the conventional endpoint.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no rel=canonical on home, category, or detail templates; /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404. robots.txt is present and the tested unknown route correctly returned HTTP 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Add self-referencing canonical links to indexable templates, publish a sitemap containing canonical public URLs, and reference it from robots.txt.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but baseline security response headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict referrer policy, and least-privilege permissions policy at the origin/CDN.

findings.summary: Sensitive browsing activity is sent to third parties, including a counter that sets third-party cookies.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 10 third-party requests and 81,737 transferred bytes across four external origins; Lighthouse identified counter.yadro.ru FTID and VID cookies. No consent or privacy choice appeared on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove non-essential third parties, gate analytics/advertising behind an informed choice, proxy or self-host essential assets, and use cookieless aggregate measurement.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, or CSP; no policy constrained the observed third-party surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and HSTS; adopt a nonce/hash CSP and evaluate Trusted Types for script-sensitive surfaces.

findings.summary: The site advertises standalone installation but does not provide a complete installable/offline experience.
findings.evidence: A manifest link exists and manifest.json declares display:"standalone", but it has no name, icons, or start_url; the service-worker probe found zero registrations and no controller.
findings.suggestedFix: Either remove the misleading app manifest or complete it with identity, icons, start_url, scope and a service worker that supplies an offline fallback.

findings.summary: The English language is declared, but layout CSS is not translation/bidirectionality ready.
findings.evidence: The document has lang=en, but CSS inspection found zero logical-property usage and 39 physical left/right declarations, including drawer positioning and spacing.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain accurate lang, add dir handling, replace physical spacing/inset declarations with logical properties, and test an RTL/long-string locale.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not format- or density-responsive.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 100 legacy JPG/PNG images, no modern-format samples, and 97 images without srcset; Lighthouse found low-resolution thumbnails being upscaled.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP plus fallback variants, provide srcset/sizes, and select dimensions that match each card/container density.
